S=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{4}\right)}{2n\pi}\;
      \frac{\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right)}{5n\pi}
\qquad (n\neq0)
\]

---

### 1.  Simplify the constant factor  

\[
S=\frac1{10\pi^{2}}\sum_{n\neq0}\frac{\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{4}\right)
                                   \sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right)}{n^{2}}.
\]

Since \(\sin(-x)=-\sin x\), the product of the two sines is even:
\(\sin(-n\pi/4)\sin(-n\pi/6)=\sin(n\pi/4)\sin(n\pi/6)\).
Hence the terms for \(n\) and \(-n\) are equal, and

\[
S=\frac{2}{10\pi^{2}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
   \frac{\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{4}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right)}{n^{2}}
   =\frac{1}{5\pi^{2}}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
   \frac{\sin (na)\,\sin (nb)}{n^{2}},\qquad
   a=\frac{\pi}{4},\; b=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]

---

### 2.  Use \(\sin a\sin b = \frac12\big[\cos(a-b)-\cos(a+b)\big]\)

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(na)\sin(nb)}{n^{2}}
   =\frac12\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
     \frac{\cos\big(n(a-b)\big)-\cos\big(n(a+b)\big)}{n^{2}} .
\]

Let  

\[
\Delta = a-b = \frac{\pi}{12},\qquad
\Sigma = a+b = \frac{5\pi}{12}.
\]

---

### 3.  The known series  

For \(0\le \theta\le 2\pi\),

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\cos(n\theta)}{n^{2}}
= \frac{\pi^{2}}{6}-\frac{\pi\theta}{2}+\frac{\theta^{2}}{4}.
\]

Apply this to \(\theta=\Delta\) and \(\theta=\Sigma\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(\Delta)&=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6}-\frac{\pi(\pi/12)}{2}
          +\frac{(\pi/12)^{2}}{4}
        =\frac{73\pi^{2}}{576},\\[4pt]
f(\Sigma)&=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6}-\frac{\pi(5\pi/12)}{2}
          +\frac{(5\pi/12)^{2}}{4}
        =\frac{\pi^{2}}{576}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(na)\sin(nb)}{n^{2}}
 =\frac12\bigl[f(\Delta)-f(\Sigma)\bigr]
 =\frac12\Bigl(\frac{73\pi^{2}}{576}-\frac{\pi^{2}}{576}\Bigr)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac{72\pi^{2}}{576}
 =\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}.
\]

---

### 4.  Insert back into \(S\)

\[
S=\frac{1}{5\pi^{2}}\cdot\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}
   =\frac{1}{80}.
\]

---
